INTERNAL MEMO: POLICY 402-B – PLAN MIGRATION & PRORATION
Date: October 15, 2023
Author: Legal & Compliance Department

Summary:
This policy governs changes to existing mobile service plans. Key provisions include:
1. Eligibility: Customers must be in good standing (no unpaid balances > $0.00) and have completed their minimum contract term OR pay an Early Termination Fee (ETF). The standard ETF is $320 for postpaid accounts with remaining months.
2. Proration Logic: When a plan change occurs mid-cycle, the new rate applies immediately. The system calculates credit for unused days on the old plan and charges for used days on the new plan within the same cycle. 
   - Formula: Credit = (Old Plan Cost / Total Days in Cycle) * Unused Days.
   - Charge = (New Plan Cost / Total Days in Cycle) * Used Days (from effective date to end of cycle).
   - Note: One-time promotional credits are NOT prorated; they remain valid until expiration regardless of plan change.
3. Billing Cycles: Standard cycles run from the 1st to the last day of the month. If a change occurs after the 15th, it may be scheduled for the next cycle unless 'Immediate Activation' is selected, which triggers proration.
4. Data Add-ons: Temporary data boosters expire at the end of the current billing cycle automatically. They cannot be carried over to a new plan if the change is immediate.

CASE FILE: TICKET #89421-XYZ
Customer: Jordan Smith
Account ID: 77429100
Phone Number: (555) 019-2834
Current Date: November 18, 2023

Ticket Description:
Customer calls requesting to downgrade from "Premium Unlimited Plus" ($85/month) to "Essential Value" ($45/month). Customer claims they are moving abroad and only need minimal local coverage. Customer is currently on the "Premium Unlimited Plus" plan under a 24-month contract signed on May 1, 2023. There are 6 months remaining on the contract. The customer has no outstanding balance. The current billing cycle runs November 1–November 30. The customer wants the change to take effect immediately (November 18) rather than waiting for the next cycle start (December 1). 

System Log Excerpt:
[2023-11-18 10:05 AM] Account status verified: Good Standing.
[2023-11-18 10:05 AM] Contract Check: Active. Remaining Months: 6. ETF Calculation: $320 applied to final bill upon termination/change request if not waived.
[2023-11-18 10:06 AM] Promotion Check: Customer received a one-time $10 discount code "WELCOME2023" applied to previous months but expired on Nov 1. No active promo credits found.
[2023-11-18 10:07 AM] Add-on Check: Customer purchased a "Weekend Data Booster" ($5) on Nov 12. It is set to expire Nov 30. 
[2023-11-18 10:10 AM] Action Taken: Representative processed "Immediate Plan Change" to Essential Value ($45/mo). System flagged potential proration error due to add-on conflict.

Email Thread between Rep (Alex Chen) and Supervisor (Maria Garcia):
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@telco.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@telco.com>
Date: Nov 18, 2023, 10:15 AM
Subject: RE: Ticket 89421-XYZ Proration Question

Hi Maria,
I just processed Jordan Smith’s downgrade to Essential Value effective today (Nov 18). The customer is annoyed about the $320 ETF because they didn't realize downgrading counts as breaking the contract. I confirmed the ETF is mandatory per Policy 402-B since they are still in contract.

My question is regarding the bill. Should I charge them the full $45 for the new plan plus the $320 ETF? Or do I prorate the $45 for the remaining 12 days (Nov 18-30)? Also, what happens to the $5 Weekend Data Booster they bought last week? Does that get refunded or kept?

Thanks,
Alex

From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@telco.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@telco.com>
Date: Nov 18, 2023, 10:22 AM
Subject: RE: Ticket 89421-XYZ Proration Question

Alex,
Good catch on the ETF. Yes, apply the $320 ETF. It is non-negotiable.
Regarding proration: Follow Policy 402-B strictly. Since the change was immediate, we prorate both the old and new plans. 
- Old Plan ($85): Prorated credit for unused days (Nov 18-30).
- New Plan ($45): Prorated charge for used days (Nov 18-30).
- Add-ons: Per Section 4, temporary boosters expire at cycle end. Do NOT refund the $5 booster cost. It remains valid until Nov 30 even though the base plan changed, but no new boosters can be added under the new plan until Dec 1.

POLICY EXCERPT: CityPower Billing Adjustment Protocol (Rev. 4.2)
Section 3.1: General Overcharge Refund. If a customer proves they were billed for services not rendered, or if the meter reading is confirmed to be erroneous by an independent technician, the full difference between the charged amount and the correct usage cost must be refunded.
Section 3.2: The 'Good Faith' Exception. Notwithstanding Section 3.1, refunds are denied if the billing error was caused by a customer's failure to provide accurate self-reported readings during the period in question, AND the total overcharge exceeds $50.00. In such cases, the customer is liable for the actual usage cost only if it can be proven that the actual usage was less than what was reported.
Section 4.0: Dispute Timeline. Claims must be filed within 60 days of the bill date. Late claims are automatically rejected unless accompanied by proof of hospitalization exceeding 14 consecutive days.

CASE FACTS:
Customer: Elias Thorne
Account Number: CP-8892-X
Bill Date: November 15, 2023
Dispute Filed: January 20, 2024
Claimed Amount in Dispute: $145.00 (Charged vs. Expected $60.00)

EVIDENCE LOG:
1. Customer Statement (Jan 20, 2024): "I noticed my December bill was high. I checked my online account history. For October and November, I manually entered estimates because I couldn't read the analog dial clearly due to poor lighting. I estimated 400 kWh each month. The system then generated bills based on these estimates. When the actual meter reader came in December, he recorded 180 kWh for the combined Oct-Nov period. The bill for Dec showed a catch-up charge of $145.00 for the previous two months. I believe this is wrong because I was told estimates are just placeholders."
2. Technician Log (Dec 12, 2023): "Meter reading verified as 180 kWh for Oct/Nov period. Previous entries were marked 'Customer Self-Report'. Customer admitted via phone chat transcript that they guessed numbers. No physical obstruction prevented them from reading the meter; they simply claimed difficulty seeing. Actual usage was significantly lower than self-reported estimates."
3. Medical Record Submission (Feb 2, 2024): Customer submitted a doctor's note stating they were hospitalized from Jan 10 to Jan 15, 2024 (5 days). This note was submitted after the dispute deadline but before the final decision.
4. Internal Ticket Note (Jan 25, 2024): "Agent Review: Bill date Nov 15. Dispute filed Jan 20. Days elapsed: 66. Deadline missed. Medical exception requires >14 days hospitalization. Customer provided 5-day note. Rejected on timeline grounds initially. However, re-evaluating merit under Section 3.2."

q1.instructions: Based on the Policy Excerpt and Case Facts, what is the final determination regarding Elias Thorne's refund claim?

criteria.refund_denied_timeline: Refund denied solely because the claim was filed 66 days after the bill date, exceeding the 60-day limit.
criteria.refund_denied_exception: Refund denied because the overcharge exceeded $50 and resulted from customer self-reporting errors, triggering the Good Faith Exception.
criteria.partial_refund: Partial refund issued for the difference between estimated and actual usage minus a service fee.
criteria.insufficient_information: Cannot determine outcome without knowing if the customer had prior disputes.

q2.instructions: Does the customer's submission of the medical record satisfy the exception required to bypass the Section 4.0 Dispute Timeline restriction?

criteria.false: The medical record does not meet the minimum duration requirement for a late filing exception.

criteria: Argument is weak: Policy explicitly places liability on customer for self-report errors exceeding $50, and technician notes confirm no physical obstruction existed.
Argument is moderate: While policy is strict, the ambiguity of 'poor lighting' creates reasonable doubt about intent.
Argument is strong: Customers are generally protected from billing errors regardless of source, making the exception invalid.
Insufficient Information: Cannot judge strength without knowing if the meter was actually unreadable.

INTERNAL MEMORANDUM: Warehouse Discrepancy Protocol v4.2

1. DEFINITION OF DISCREPANCY TYPES:
- Systematic Error: A recurring deviation caused by faulty scanning equipment, software bugs, or consistent human procedural error affecting multiple SKUs over time.
- Isolated Incident: A single event causing a variance, typically due to theft, accidental damage, or misplacement of a specific item batch.
- Cycle Count Variance: The difference between the physical count and the theoretical system inventory during scheduled cycle counts.

2. THRESHOLD FOR ESCALATION:
- Any discrepancy exceeding $500 in total value must be escalated to Regional Operations Director within 24 hours.
- Discrepancies under $500 are handled at the Site Manager level but must be logged in the WMS (Warehouse Management System).
- Critical Safety Items (CSIs): If the discrepancy involves items classified as CSIs (e.g., hazardous materials, high-value electronics >$10k), immediate escalation is required regardless of dollar value.

3. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS REQUIREMENTS:
- Before closing a ticket, the investigator must determine if the issue is Systematic or Isolated.
- Evidence for Systematic Error requires correlation across at least three distinct shifts or two different SKU categories within the last 7 days.
- Evidence for Isolated Incident requires proof that neighboring bins/SKUs had zero variance during the same audit period.

---

CASE FILE: WH-2024-0892
DATE: October 14, 2023
LOCATION: Distribution Center B, Zone 4 (Electronics)
ITEM: Wireless Noise-Cancelling Headphones (SKU: NC-HDP-99)
UNIT COST: $120.00
SYSTEM QUANTITY BEFORE COUNT: 50 units
PHYSICAL COUNT: 46 units
VARIANCE: -4 units ($480.00 total value)

TICKET LOG:
[10/12 09:00] Audit initiated by J. Miller (Site Manager). Zone 4 cycle count begins.
[10/12 10:30] Variance detected on SKU NC-HDP-99. Bin 4A-12 shows 46 units; WMS expects 50.
[10/12 10:35] J. Miller flags potential theft. Security camera review requested for Bin 4A-12 access logs from 10/01 to 10/12.
[10/12 14:00] Security report submitted. Camera footage confirms only authorized personnel accessed Bin 4A-12. No unlogged removals observed. Footage quality degraded after 10/05 due to known lens smudge issue (Ticket MAINT-2023-441).
[10/12 15:00] J. Miller expands scope. Checks adjacent bin 4A-13 (SKU: Wired Headsets). Variance: 0 units. Checks bin 4B-01 (SKU: Bluetooth Speakers). Variance: -2 units ($150 value).
[10/13 09:00] Investigation continues. Review of receiving logs for Oct 1-5. All inbound shipments scanned correctly via automated conveyor scanner Model X-200.
[10/13 11:00] Maintenance Ticket MAINT-2023-441 closed. Cause identified: Dust accumulation on scanner lens of Conveyor Belt Line 3, which services Zone 4. Calibration records show Line 3 scanners were out of spec for tolerance +/- 0.5% starting Oct 1.
[10/13 12:00] Data Analyst R. Singh pulls historical data. Over the last 7 days, Zone 4 received 4 shipments via Conveyor Line 3. Total expected intake: 200 units of various small electronics. Physical recount reveals a net deficit of 12 units across 5 different SKUs (including NC-HDP-99 and Bluetooth Speakers).
[10/13 14:00] J. Miller drafts preliminary conclusion. Suspects internal theft based on initial lack of camera clarity. Proposes terminating security contract.
[10/14 09:00] Regional Director M. Lewis reviews draft. Questions the 'Theft' hypothesis given the clean camera logs for authorized personnel and the concurrent variance in other SKUs serviced by the same faulty conveyor line.

EMAIL THREAD:

To: J. Miller <j.miller@company.com>, R. Singh <r.singh@company.com>
Subject: RE: WH-2024-0892 Preliminary Findings

J.,
Please hold off on any personnel actions. R. Singh's data indicates a pattern across multiple SKUs served by Conveyor Line 3. This suggests a systematic scanning error rather than isolated theft. The maintenance ticket confirms the scanner was out of calibration during the exact window of the discrepancies.

Requirement: We need to classify this incident officially. Does this meet the criteria for 'Systematic Error' per Protocol v4.2? Also, does this require escalation to my desk immediately, or can you close it locally?

Thanks,
M.

criteria.systematic_error: Meets all criteria for systematic error

DOCUMENTO: Política de Gestão de Fiança Bancária e Caução (Versão 2.3, vigente desde 01/01/2024)

1. Definições: A 'Caução' é um valor depositado pelo inquilino no início da locação para cobrir danos ou inadimplência. A 'Fiança Bancária' é uma garantia oferecida por instituição financeira.

2. Prazo de Restituição: O valor da caução deve ser devolvido ao inquilino em até 30 (trinta) dias corridos após a vistoria final e entrega das chaves, desde que não haja pendências financeiras ou estruturais apontadas no laudo técnico.

3. Critérios de Desconto:
   a) Danos Estruturais: Riscos profundos, buracos na parede, janelas quebradas ou piso danificado resultam em desconto integral do custo de reparo estimado pela empresa contratada.
   b) Sujeira Excessiva: Se a limpeza profissional for necessária devido à negligência comprovada (ex.: gordura incrustada em coifa, mofo por falta de ventilação), o custo será descontado da caução. Limpeza padrão não gera desconto.
   c) Multa por Rescisão Antecipada: Em caso de quebra de contrato antes do prazo mínimo de 12 meses, aplica-se multa proporcional aos meses restantes, deduzida da caução.

---

QUALITY CONTROL POLICY EXCERPT: DEFECT CLASSIFICATION AND RELEASE PROTOCOLS (Rev. 4.2)

1. CRITICAL DEFECTS: Any defect that compromises the safety, regulatory compliance, or primary function of the product. Critical defects result in immediate quarantine and mandatory destruction of the affected batch unless a formal Engineering Change Request (ECR) is approved by the Chief Quality Officer (CQO). Deviations are not permitted for critical defects under any circumstances.

2. MAJOR DEFECTS: Defects that affect usability, reliability, or appearance but do not compromise safety or primary function. Major defects may be released via 'Use-As-Is' (UAI) disposition if: (a) The defect rate is below 2.0% of the total batch quantity; (b) A Customer Notification Form (CNF) has been signed by the account manager; and (c) No more than two consecutive batches from the same production line have been released with UAI dispositions in the last 90 days.

3. MINOR DEFECTS: Cosmetic flaws or non-functional deviations that do not impact performance. Minor defects can be released without customer notification provided the overall Acceptable Quality Level (AQL) remains within ISO 2859-1 standards.

4. REWORK PROTOCOL: Reworked items must undergo full re-inspection. If a batch contains mixed critical and major defects, the entire batch is treated as critical. Partial releases are prohibited.

INTERNAL MEMO: PRESCRIPTION REFILL POLICY UPDATE
Date: October 14, 2023
From: Sarah Jenkins, Clinical Director, MedCare Pharmacy
To: All Pharmacist Staff
Re: Controlled Substance Refill Restrictions and Prior Authorization Exceptions

Effective November 1, 2023, the following protocols apply to all Schedule II-V medications. Note that Schedule II drugs cannot be refilled; they require a new prescription. For Schedule III-V drugs, standard refill limits apply unless specific exceptions are met.

SECTION 1: STANDARD REFILL LIMITS
- Schedule III & IV: Maximum of 5 refills within 6 months from the date written. After 6 months or 5 refills, a new prescription is required.
- Schedule V: Maximum of 5 refills within 12 months.

SECTION 2: PRIOR AUTHORIZATION (PA) EXCEPTIONS
A PA is required if:
1. The patient has reached their maximum refill limit for a Schedule III-V drug before the expiration date of the original prescription, AND
2. The treating physician submits a clinical justification form (Form 7B) detailing why early renewal is medically necessary.

SECTION 3: EARLY REFILL PROTOCOLS
Pharmacists may dispense an early refill only under the following conditions:
A. Emergency Situations: Defined as acute pain exacerbation or loss of medication due to theft/loss, verified by police report or ER discharge summary.
B. Insurance Mandates: If the patient’s insurance plan mandates a 30-day supply but the doctor wrote a 90-day quantity, we may split the fill upon approval from the Regional Compliance Officer (RCO).
C. Patient Convenience: Early refills for vacation/travel are NOT permitted for controlled substances without a PA.

SECTION 4: VIOLATION GRADING SCALE
Internal audits will grade compliance failures on a severity scale:
Level 1 (Low): Administrative error, e.g., wrong label printed but correct drug given, no patient harm.
Level 2 (Medium): Dispensing without verifying ID for Schedule III, but within refill limits.
Level 3 (High): Dispensing a controlled substance outside of legal refill limits (e.g., giving a 6th refill on a 5-refill max script) OR dispensing without a required PA when Form 7B was missing.
Level 4 (Critical): Dispensing Schedule II with no valid current prescription, or falsifying records.

CUSTOMS CLEARANCE AND DEMURRAGE POLICY EXCERPT
Effective 1 January 2024

Section 4.2 — Importer of Record Obligations. The importer of record (IOR) must submit a complete customs entry package no later than 5 business days after vessel discharge. A package is complete only if it includes a commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and a certificate of origin where preferential duty treatment is claimed. Incomplete packages are rejected and the 5-day clock restarts from the date of rejection notice, not from the original discharge date.

Section 4.7 — Demurrage Liability. Demurrage accrues at USD 185 per container per calendar day beginning on the first calendar day after the free-time period expires. Free time is 7 calendar days from discharge for standard dry containers, and 5 calendar days for refrigerated containers. Demurrage is waived only when the delay is caused solely by a customs authority hold, and the IOR provides a written hold notice within 48 hours of the hold. A carrier-side equipment shortage does not qualify for waiver.

Section 5.1 — Negation of Preferential Treatment. A certificate of origin does not confer preferential duty treatment if the goods were not wholly obtained or substantially transformed in the named country. The mere issuance of a certificate by a chamber of commerce does not establish origin.

---

CASE FACTS

Vessel MV Nordstar discharged 3 containers at Port of Halewood on Monday, 4 March 2024.
- Container HLXU-4412 (dry, standard): commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading present; certificate of origin absent.
- Container RFFU-8890 (refrigerated): full package present including certificate of origin for preferential treatment.
- Container DRYU-2201 (dry, standard): full package present.

On 5 March 2024, a customs authority hold was placed on RFFU-8890. The IOR, Kestrel Imports Ltd., received the hold notice that same day but did not send written notice to the carrier until 10 March 2024.

On 7 March 2024, Kestrel submitted HLXU-4412's package without the certificate of origin. The customs broker, Bayline Logistics, rejected it on 8 March 2024 by email, noting the missing certificate.

Email thread:

From: ops@kestrelimports.com
To: broker@baylinelogistics.com
Date: 8 March 2024, 09:14
Subject: RE: HLXU-4412 rejection
We can get the certificate of origin from the supplier in Manila. Does the 5-day clock restart from your rejection notice?

From: broker@baylinelogistics.com
To: ops@kestrelimports.com
Date: 8 March 2024, 11:02
Subject: RE: HLXU-4412 rejection
Yes, under Section 4.2 the clock restarts from rejection notice. Also, note your refrigerated container RFFU-8890 has a customs hold. If you want demurrage waived, send us the hold notice in writing within 48 hours of the hold.

From: ops@kestrelimports.com
To: broker@baylinelogistics.com
Date: 10 March 2024, 16:40
Subject: RE: RFFU-8890 hold
Apologies for the delay. Here is the written hold notice, attached. We did not send it earlier because we assumed the carrier already knew about the hold.

Ticket T-88231 (opened 12 March 2024):
Customer reports DRYU-2201 was released from the terminal on 11 March 2024. No demurrage invoice received yet.

Log excerpt:
- 4 Mar 2024: discharge all three containers.
- 5 Mar 2024: customs hold placed on RFFU-8890. IOR notified same day.
- 8 Mar 2024: HLXU-4412 package rejected for missing certificate of origin.
- 10 Mar 2024: IOR sends written hold notice for RFFU-8890.
- 11 Mar 2024: DRYU-2201 picked up from terminal.
- 12 Mar 2024: ticket T-88231 opened regarding DRYU-2201 demurrage invoice.

Additional context: The certificate of origin for RFFU-8890 states the goods were manufactured in Vietnam. The commercial invoice shows the goods were assembled in Thailand from Vietnamese and Cambodian components. No substantial transformation occurred in Vietnam. Kestrel assumed the certificate alone guaranteed preferential treatment.

Carrier-side equipment shortage was reported at the terminal on 6 March 2024, affecting dry containers only. DRYU-2201 was not affected; it was available for pickup from 5 March 2024.

---

QUESTION CONTEXT FOR EVALUATION ONLY (not part of the document):
All dates are in 2024. Business days exclude weekends. 4 March 2024 is a Monday. 5 March is Tuesday. 8 March is Friday. 10 March is Sunday. 11 March is Monday. 12 March is Tuesday. No public holidays occur in this period.

criteria.confers_preferential_treatment: It confers preferential duty treatment because a chamber of commerce issued it.
criteria.does_not_confer_preferential_treatment: It does not confer preferential duty treatment because no substantial transformation occurred in the named country.

criteria: Completely accurate: the clock restarts from discharge, and 11 March is within 5 business days.

A residential building permit application is complete only when all of the following are on file: (a) signed application form; (b) site plan drawn to scale; (c) two copies of construction drawings stamped by a licensed architect or engineer; (d) proof of workers' compensation coverage; (e) stormwater management affidavit.
2. General rule: A completeness review is performed within 10 business days of intake, and the 10-day clock starts on the date the fee is paid.
3. Exception overriding Section 2: For applications filed under the expedited accessory-dwelling-unit (ADU) program, the 10-day clock starts on the date of intake, not the date the fee is paid.
4. Exception overriding Section 3: If an expedited ADU application is missing the stormwater management affidavit, the expedited track is suspended and the application is processed under the standard 10-day rule in Section 2.
5. A review is not "complete" until every item in Section 1 is on file; missing items are noted on the deficiency notice, and the applicant has 30 calendar days from notice to cure.

CASE FACTS
Applicant: Dolores Nakamura, 412 Alder Court. Application no. BP-2024-0871, a detached ADU (garage conversion), filed under the expedited ADU program. Intake date: Monday, April 8, 2024. Permit fee paid: Thursday, April 11, 2024.

SEÇÃO 3.2 - Classificação de Severidade:
- CRÍTICA: Risco imediato à segurança do usuário final ou falha funcional catastrófica que impede a operação principal. Exige retenção total e investigação de causa raiz formal (8D). Nível de prioridade: P1.
- MAJOR: Falha funcional que degrada significativamente o desempenho ou reduz a vida útil, mas não compromete a segurança imediata nem impede a função primária. Permite liberação condicional com desvio aprovado pelo Gerente de Qualidade e Engenheiro de Produto. Nível de prioridade: P2.
- MINOR: Desvio cosmético ou dimensional fora de tolerância sem impacto funcional perceptível ao cliente final. Pode ser liberado por inspetor de qualidade sênior após verificação visual. Nível de prioridade: P3.

MERIDIAN FREIGHT FORWARDING LTD — CUSTOMS CLEARANCE POLICY EXCERPT (Rev. 2024-11)

3.2 Duty Drawback Eligibility
A consignee may claim duty drawback only if the imported goods were not used in the United States before export. Goods that entered a foreign-trade zone (FTZ) and remained in privileged foreign status are not considered to have been entered for consumption. However, if the goods were withdrawn from the FTZ for consumption and later exported, no drawback is available unless the consignee files a protest within 90 days of liquidation. Under no circumstances shall a drawback claim be filed on goods that were sold at retail before export.

3.7 Record Retention
All commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, and entry summaries must be retained for five years from the date of entry. Missing documents must be reconstructed within 30 days of a CBP request. Failure to produce records may result in penalties under 19 U.S.C. § 1592.

4.1 Post-Entry Amendments
A post-entry amendment (PEA) may be filed to correct errors in value, classification, or quantity. PEAs must be filed within 300 days of the entry date. A protest under 19 U.S.C. § 1514 must be filed within 180 days of liquidation. Neither a PEA nor a protest is required if the error is de minimis (less than $20 in duty).

5.3 Forced Labor Screening
All shipments from entities on the UFLPA Entity List are subject to detention. A shipment may be released only if the importer provides clear and convincing evidence that the goods were not mined, produced, or manufactured wholly or in part in Xinjiang. If the importer does not respond within 30 days, the shipment is excluded.

CASE FACTS — ENTRY NO. 7501-2024-08841
Consignee: Northwind Components Inc., 4400 Harbor Blvd, Long Beach, CA.
Importer of record: Northwind Components Inc.
Entry date: 2024-03-12. Liquidation date: 2024-09-15.
Port of entry: Los Angeles (2704).
Goods: 1,200 lithium-ion battery packs, HTS 8507.60.0020, entered value $84,000. Duty rate 3.4% ad valorem = $2,856.

On 2024-04-02, Northwind filed a PEA to correct the value from $84,000 to $79,500 because the invoice had included a $4,500 freight charge that should have been non-dutiable. The port accepted the PEA and reliquidated on 2024-06-01, reducing duty to $2,703. The difference of $153 was refunded.

On 2024-08-10, Northwind exported 300 of the battery packs to a buyer in Canada. These 300 packs had been entered for consumption on 2024-03-12 and were never placed in an FTZ. Northwind filed a drawback claim on 2024-08-20 for the duty paid on those 300 packs, claiming $675.75 (300/1200 × $2,703).

On 2024-09-01, CBP sent a request for records: commercial invoice, packing list, and bill of lading. Northwind provided the commercial invoice and packing list on 2024-09-20, but the bill of lading was missing. Northwind’s customs broker, Pacific Trade Services, emailed Northwind on 2024-09-21: 'We can reconstruct the B/L from the carrier’s manifest, but it will take 45 days. CBP will not grant an extension beyond 30 days from the request.'

On 2024-09-25, CBP detained a separate shipment from Northwind (Entry 7501-2024-09992) because the manufacturer, GreenVolt Ltd., appeared on the UFLPA Entity List. The detention notice stated: 'Importer must provide clear and convincing evidence that the goods were not mined, produced, or manufactured wholly or in part in Xinjiang.' Northwind’s compliance officer, Dana Ruiz, sent a response on 2024-10-20 with a certificate of origin from GreenVolt stating the battery cells were assembled in Malaysia, but the anode material was sourced from a supplier in Xinjiang. The response did not include any evidence tracing the anode material to a non-Xinjiang source.

EMAIL THREAD — 2024-10-22
From: Dana Ruiz
To: Pacific Trade Services
Subject: Entry 08841 drawback and records
'We filed the drawback on the 300 exported packs. CBP hasn’t paid it yet. Also, we still don’t have the B/L for the 2024-03-12 entry. Can we just send the manifest copy? And what about the GreenVolt shipment — are we going to lose it?'

From: Pacific Trade Services
To: Dana Ruiz
'On the drawback: since the packs were entered for consumption and then exported, and they were never in an FTZ, I think the claim is invalid unless you filed a protest. You didn’t file a protest. On the B/L: CBP requested it on 2024-09-01. You have 30 days from the request to reconstruct. That deadline passed on 2024-10-01. On GreenVolt: your response on 2024-10-20 was after the 30-day deadline (which was 2024-10-25). You did respond, but you didn’t provide clear and convincing evidence because the anode material is from Xinjiang. So the shipment will likely be excluded.'

TICKET — CBP PORT 2704
Ticket 2024-10-25-08841: 'Drawback claim for Entry 7501-2024-08841. Claimant exported 300 units on 2024-08-10. Were goods in FTZ? No. Was protest filed? No. Was entry liquidated? Yes, 2024-09-15. Claim amount: $675.75. Status: Under review.'

q1.instructions: Based on the policy and case facts, what is the correct disposition of Northwind's drawback claim for the 300 exported battery packs?

criteria.grant_full: Grant the full drawback claim of $675.75 because the goods were exported and duty was paid.
criteria.deny_no_protest: Deny the claim because the goods were entered for consumption and later exported, and no protest was filed within the required period.
criteria.grant_partial: Grant a partial drawback of $153 because only the PEA-refunded duty qualifies.
criteria.deny_ftz: Deny the claim because the goods were not in an FTZ.
criteria.insufficient_information: There is insufficient information to determine the disposition.

q2.instructions: True or false: Northwind's response to the UFLPA detention on 2024-10-20 satisfied the requirement to provide clear and convincing evidence that the goods were not mined, produced, or manufactured wholly or in part in Xinjiang.

criteria.true: The response satisfied the requirement because it included a certificate of origin showing assembly in Malaysia.
criteria.false: The response did not satisfy the requirement because the anode material was sourced from Xinjiang and no evidence traced it to a non-Xinjiang source.

criteria.pea_late: The PEA filed on 2024-04-02 was late because it was more than 300 days after entry.

MEMORANDUM
TO: Project Managers, Compliance Officers
FROM: Department of Building Safety
DATE: October 15, 2023
SUBJECT: Revised Checklist for Commercial Renovation Permits (CRP-2024)

Effective November 1, 2023, all commercial renovation permit applications must adhere to the updated CRP-2024 checklist. This revision streamlines review by prioritizing structural integrity documentation and energy compliance. The previous CRP-2023 checklist is obsolete for applications submitted on or after this date.

REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION:
1. Site Plan & Elevation Drawings: Must be stamped by a licensed architect within the last 6 months.
2. Structural Calculation Package: Required if load-bearing walls are removed or modified. Must include soil report dated within 12 months of application submission.
3. Energy Compliance Form EC-9: Mandatory for projects exceeding $50,000 in material costs. If project cost is below $50,000, a simplified De-minimis Exemption form may be filed instead.
4. Contractor License Verification: Current license number and insurance certificate valid through the estimated completion date.

TIMELINE AND DEADLINES:
- Standard Review Period: 20 business days from complete submission.
- Expedited Review: Available for an additional fee of $1,500; reduces standard period to 7 business days.
- Resubmission Window: If deficiencies are noted, applicants have 10 calendar days from the notice date to cure defects. Failure to resubmit within this window results in automatic denial without further notice.

CASE FILE #8842-B: 'The Oak Street Bistro' Renovation
Application Submitted: November 5, 2023
Project Manager: Sarah Jenkins
General Contractor: Apex Build Co.
Estimated Material Cost: $48,500
Scope of Work: Removal of one non-load-bearing partition wall; installation of new HVAC ducting; facade repair.

TICKET LOG:
[Nov 06] Application received. Assigned to Reviewer A.
[Nov 12] Deficiency Notice Issued: 
   - Issue 1: Soil report provided is dated June 1, 2022.
   - Issue 2: Missing Energy Compliance Form EC-9.
   - Note: Partition wall removal does not require structural calculations per Section 4.2, but soil report validity affects foundation stability assessment for HVAC mounting.
[Nov 13] Email from Sarah Jenkins to Reviewer A:
"Hi Team,
We received the deficiency notice yesterday. Regarding Issue 1, we believe the soil report is still valid because no excavation occurred since then. Regarding Issue 2, our material cost is only $48,500, which is under the $50,000 threshold mentioned in your policy memo. We plan to submit the simplified De-minimis Exemption form. Please confirm if we can proceed with just that form. We will upload documents by November 20th.
Best,
Sarah"
[Nov 14] Response from Reviewer A:
"Dear Ms. Jenkins,
The policy states the soil report must be dated within 12 months of APPLICATION SUBMISSION. Your application was submitted Nov 5, 2023. A June 2022 report is older than 12 months (it expired May 31, 2023). You must provide a current report. Regarding the Energy form, while the cost is under $50k, the installation of new HVAC ducting constitutes a mechanical system modification requiring full EC-9 compliance regardless of cost, per Technical Bulletin TB-23-04 which overrides the general cost threshold. Please correct both items."
[Nov 15] Internal Note: Applicant has until Nov 22, 2023, to cure defects based on the Nov 12 notice.

q1.instructions: Based on the correspondence and policy, what is the specific reason Reviewer A rejected the applicant's proposed solution for the Energy Compliance requirement?

criteria.a: The applicant failed to pay the expedited review fee required for mechanical modifications.
criteria.b: The soil report expiration invalidated the entire application including energy forms.
criteria.c: Technical Bulletin TB-23-04 mandates full EC-9 compliance for HVAC installations irrespective of cost thresholds.
criteria.d: The De-minimis Exemption form is only available for residential projects under $50,000.
criteria.e: The application was submitted after the effective date of the revised checklist.

q3.instructions: Evaluate the completeness of the applicant's initial submission against the CRP-2024 requirements using the following scale: 0=Missing Critical Items, 1=Partial/Deficient, 2=Complete.
criteria: Level 0: Application missing site plans or contractor license entirely.
Level 1: Application included basic forms but lacked required technical attachments like valid soil reports or correct energy forms.
Level 2: All documents were present, valid, and compliant with the specific project scope at time of submission.

'Para produtos secos não refrigerados, a temperatura ambiente deve ser monitorada duas vezes ao dia (manhã e tarde). A conformidade exige que o registro seja feito em até 15 minutos após a medição física. Não é permitido registrar valores antes da confirmação visual do termômetro. Um atraso na digitação superior a 60 minutos invalida a entrada para fins de auditoria imediata, embora possa ser aceita com justificativa formal se houver falha técnica comprovada no sistema.

POLICY EXCERPT: MediSafe Pharmacy Refill Protocol (v2.4)
1. Controlled Substances (Schedule II-V): No early refills permitted under any circumstance, including travel or lost medication. Requests before 28 days from fill date are automatically denied.
2. Non-Controlled Maintenance Meds: Early refill allowed if patient travels >50 miles for >7 days. Proof of travel (ticket/itinerary) required in notes.
3. Insurance Limitations: If insurance denies payment, pharmacist may override to cash price only if patient has active loyalty membership (Gold tier).

CASE LOG: Ticket #8921
Patient: John Doe (DOB: 1985-03-12)
Medication: Alprazolam 0.5mg (Schedule IV), Qty 30, Day Supply: 30 days.
Last Fill Date: 2023-10-01.
Request Date: 2023-10-20.
Pharmacist Note: Patient claims they are flying to Europe on 2023-10-25 for a 14-day vacation. They state they misplaced their current bottle. They provided a screenshot of an airline confirmation email dated 2023-09-15 showing departure from JFK to London Heathrow. The patient is enrolled in the Gold Loyalty Program since 2021.
System Action: Auto-denial triggered due to Schedule IV status and request <28 days after fill.
Email Thread:
Patient: "I have my ticket! Please let me pick it up today so I don't run out." 
Pharmacist Sarah: "Mr. Doe, I understand your concern. However, our policy strictly prohibits early refills for controlled substances like Alprazolam, regardless of travel plans or loyalty status. We cannot dispense until Oct 29th."

q1.instructions: What was the primary reason for the system's automatic denial of the refill request?

criteria.controlled_substance_early_refill: The medication is a controlled substance and the request was made less than 28 days after the last fill.
criteria.insurance_coverage_issue: The patient's insurance plan did not cover early refills for travel purposes.
criteria.missing_travel_proof: The pharmacist rejected the screenshot as insufficient proof of travel distance.
criteria.loyalty_tier_insufficient: The patient's Gold tier status does not grant exceptions for Schedule IV drugs.

q2.instructions: Could the pharmacist legally override the auto-denial using the 'Insurance Limitations' rule because the patient has Gold status?

criteria.true: Yes, Gold status allows overrides for all medications if there is a payment issue.
criteria.false: No, the Insurance Limitations rule applies only to payment denials, not controlled substance safety policies.

DOCUMENTO: Procedimento Operacional Padrão (POP) – Gestão de Divergências de Inventário – Armazém Central da LogiBrasil Distribuidora S.A. – Versão 3.2, vigente a partir de 01/07/2024.

1. OBJETIVO: Estabelecer critérios para identificação, registro, tratamento e aprovação de ajustes de inventário no Armazém Central.

2. DEFINIÇÕES:
2.1. Divergência de inventário: diferença entre a quantidade física contada e a quantidade registrada no Sistema de Gestão de Estoque (SGE) para um mesmo SKU e lote.
2.2. Divergência crítica: divergência cujo valor financeiro absoluto (quantidade divergente × custo unitário) seja igual ou superior a R$ 5.000,00 (cinco mil reais).
2.3. Divergência não crítica: divergência cujo valor financeiro absoluto seja inferior a R$ 5.000,00.
2.4. Ajuste de inventário: lançamento no SGE para corrigir a quantidade registrada, após aprovação conforme alçadas.

3. ALÇADAS DE APROVAÇÃO:
3.1. Divergências não críticas: aprovação pelo Supervisor de Inventário.
3.2. Divergências críticas: aprovação obrigatória do Gerente de Operações, com ciência do Supervisor de Inventário.
3.3. Em caso de divergência crítica com indício de avaria, furto ou erro sistêmico, o Gerente de Operações deve comunicar formalmente o Gerente de Riscos e Compliance antes de autorizar o ajuste. A comunicação deve ocorrer em até 1 (um) dia útil após a identificação.

4. PRAZOS:
4.1. Toda divergência identificada em contagem cíclica deve ser registrada no ticket de inventário em até 1 (um) dia útil da contagem.
4.2. O ajuste no SGE deve ser efetivado em até 5 (cinco) dias úteis após a aprovação da alçada competente.
4.3. A contagem de inventário geral anual ocorre em 30 de junho. Divergências identificadas nessa contagem seguem o fluxo normal de aprovação e ajuste.

5. DOCUMENTAÇÃO EXIGIDA:
5.1. Ticket de inventário contendo: data da contagem, SKU, lote, quantidade contada, quantidade sistêmica, custo unitário, valor da divergência, nome do contador e nome do conferente.
5.2. Para divergências críticas: além do ticket, e-mail de aprovação do Gerente de Operações e, quando aplicável, e-mail de ciência do Gerente de Riscos e Compliance.

POLÍTICA DE RESERVA E CANCELAMENTO – RESTAURANTE 'LA MESA DOURADA' (VIGENTE DESDE 01/03/2024)

1. Escopo: Aplica-se a reservas para grupos de 6 ou mais pessoas ou mesas privativas.
2. Depósito de Garantia: É obrigatório um depósito no valor de R$ 50,00 por pessoa para confirmar a reserva. Este valor é abatido do total da conta final.
3. Prazos de Cancelamento:
   - Cancelamento com 72 horas ou mais de antecedência: Reembolso integral do depósito via PIX ou estorno no cartão original.
   - Cancelamento entre 24 e 71 horas antes: O restaurante retém 50% do depósito como taxa administrativa.
   - Cancelamento com menos de 24 horas antes ou No-Show (não comparecimento): Retenção de 100% do depósito.
4. Alterações de Data/Hora: Permitidas apenas uma vez, desde que solicitadas com pelo menos 48 horas de antecedência e mediante disponibilidade. A segunda alteração será tratada como cancelamento e nova reserva, sujeita às taxas vigentes.
5. Horário de Referência: Considera-se o horário agendado na confirmação inicial para cálculo dos prazos de cancelamento.

INTERNAL MEMO: OPEN SOURCE LICENSE COMPLIANCE REVIEW
FROM: Sarah Jenkins, Senior Legal Counsel
TO: DevOps Team Lead, Product Managers
DATE: October 24, 2023
RE: Integration of 'FastParser' Library into Project Alpha

1. POLICY EXCERPT (v4.2)
Our corporate policy strictly prohibits the inclusion of any code under licenses deemed "Copyleft" or "Reciprocal" in proprietary closed-source products. Specifically:
- GPL v2/v3: PROHIBITED in proprietary binaries unless the entire product is open-sourced.
- LGPL v2.1/v3: PERMITTED ONLY if linked dynamically and users can replace the library. Static linking is PROHIBITED.
- Apache 2.0/MIT/BSD: PERMITTED with attribution requirements.
- AGPL v3: PROHIBITED in all server-side deployments without explicit executive waiver.

2. CASE FACTS
Project Alpha is a closed-source SaaS platform. The team wishes to integrate `fast-parser-lib` version 1.4.2. This library provides high-performance CSV parsing.

The `fast-parser-lib` repository on GitHub contains two distinct components:
A) Core Parsing Engine (`src/core/`): Licensed under Apache 2.0.
B) Optional Plugin Module (`src/plugins/csv_validator.py`): Licensed under GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPLv3).

The build system currently compiles both directories into a single monolithic binary artifact named `alpha_core.so`. There is no mechanism for end-users to swap out the plugin module post-compilation. The plugin is imported at runtime via a static registry map in C++, not via dynamic loading (dlopen).

Additionally, the project uses a separate dependency, `math-utils`, licensed under MIT. A developer attempted to combine `fast-parser-lib` core (Apache 2.0) with `math-utils` (MIT) into a new file `combined_util.c`. This file is distributed as source code only, not compiled into the final binary.

3. EMAIL THREAD
From: Mike Ross (Backend Dev)
To: Sarah Jenkins
Date: Oct 23, 2023, 14:15
Subject: Urgent: FastParser integration block?

Hi Sarah,
We are blocked on the Q4 release. I see that `fast-parser-lib` has an Apache 2.0 license badge on the README. Can we just use it? The GPLv3 part is only for an optional validator that we don't even call in our main workflow. We can strip it from the repo before building.

Also, I combined the Apache code with some MIT code from another lib into one file. Is that okay?

Best,
Mike

From: Sarah Jenkins
To: Mike Ross
Date: Oct 24, 2023, 09:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: FastParser integration block?

Mike,

Regarding the stripping: If you remove the GPLv3 files entirely from the source tree used for the production build, the resulting binary contains no GPLv3 code. However, our CI pipeline logs indicate that `csv_validator.py` is still being pulled during dependency resolution because it is listed in `requirements.txt` as a transitive dependency of `data-adapter-v2`, which *is* required for the import feature. We need to confirm if `data-adapter-v2` actually imports the GPLv3 module or just lists it.

Regarding the combination: Combining Apache 2.0 and MIT code into a single source file is generally acceptable as both are permissive, provided you retain both copyright notices. However, this does not resolve the `alpha_core.so` issue.

I need a definitive answer on whether the GPLv3 code ends up in the final shipped binary. If it does, we cannot ship.

Sarah

4. TICKET LOG
Ticket #8842: Investigate Transitive Dependencies
Status: Closed
Resolution: Won't Fix
Comment by J. Doe (Security Analyst):
"Verified that `data-adapter-v2` imports `fast_parser_lib.plugins.csv_validator`. The import statement `from fast_parser_lib.plugins.csv_validator import validate_row` exists in line 45 of `adapter_main.py`. Therefore, the GPLv3 code is loaded into memory when the application starts, regardless of whether the function is called. The static linker includes the symbol table for the plugin."

5. FINAL BUILD ARTIFACT ANALYSIS
File: `alpha_core.so`
Size: 4.2 MB
License Scan Report:
- Detected: Apache 2.0 text blocks.
- Detected: MIT text blocks.
- Detected: GPLv3 text blocks in embedded string resources.
- Note: The scanner flags the presence of GPLv3 text strings but does not analyze binary instruction sets. It assumes text presence implies code presence.

q1.instructions: Based on the policy and evidence, what is the correct compliance status for shipping `alpha_core.so`?

criteria.allowed: The binary is compliant because the GPLv3 code is not executed.
criteria.prohibited_static_linking: The binary is prohibited because it statically links/includes GPLv3 code in a closed-source context.
criteria.prohibited_agpl: The binary is prohibited because it uses AGPL code.
criteria.insufficient_information: It is impossible to determine compliance without seeing the source code.

q2.instructions: Is the combination of Apache 2.0 and MIT code into `combined_util.c` a violation of company policy?

criteria.true: Yes, mixing licenses creates a compatibility conflict.
criteria.false: No, both are permissive licenses compatible with each other.

q3.instructions: Rate the severity of the compliance risk regarding the `csv_validator.py` inclusion.
criteria: Low: No risk, code is unused.
Medium: Risk exists but is mitigated by lack of execution.
High: Critical risk requiring immediate remediation due to direct incorporation of incompatible license terms.
Insufficient Evidence: Cannot assess risk.

POLÍTICA DE CLASSIFICAÇÃO DE SEVERIDADE DE INCIDENTES – VERSÃO 3.2

1. Definições:
1.1. Incidente: evento não planejado que interrompe ou degrada a qualidade de um serviço de TI.
1.2. Severidade: classificação do impacto e urgência de um incidente, determinada no momento da abertura do ticket e revisada conforme novas informações.

2. Níveis de severidade:
2.1. S1 – Crítico: indisponibilidade total de serviço essencial para a operação ou receita, afetando múltiplas áreas ou clientes externos. Tempo de resposta: 15 minutos. Tempo de resolução: 4 horas.
2.2. S2 – Alto: degradação significativa de serviço essencial, afetando uma área ou um grupo de usuários, com workaround indisponível. Tempo de resposta: 30 minutos. Tempo de resolução: 8 horas.
2.3. S3 – Médio: degradação parcial de serviço não essencial ou de serviço essencial com workaround disponível. Tempo de resposta: 2 horas. Tempo de resolução: 3 dias úteis.
2.4. S4 – Baixo: impacto mínimo, sem interrupção de serviço, dúvida ou solicitação de informação. Tempo de resposta: 1 dia útil. Tempo de resolução: 5 dias úteis.

3. Regras de classificação:
3.1. A severidade deve considerar o impacto no negócio, e não apenas o número de usuários afetados.
3.2. Incidentes que afetam sistemas de faturamento ou pagamento são automaticamente elevados em um nível, se não forem originalmente S1.
3.3. Incidentes que afetam sistemas de segurança da informação (autenticação, autorização, criptografia) são automaticamente elevados em um nível, se não forem originalmente S1.
3.4. Se houver risco de violação de dados pessoais ou dados sensíveis, a severidade mínima é S1.
3.5. Incidentes que ocorrem fora do horário comercial (19h às 8h, fins de semana e feriados) têm o tempo de resposta contado a partir do próximo horário comercial, mas a severidade não muda automaticamente.
3.6. A ausência de informação sobre impacto no negócio deve levar à classificação provisória como S3, até que mais dados estejam disponíveis.

4. Exemplos:
4.1. Portal de vendas fora do ar para todos os clientes: S1.
4.2. Lentidão no sistema de RH afetando 20 usuários, sem workaround: S2.
4.3. Erro intermitente no sistema de relatórios, com workaround: S3.
4.4. Dúvida sobre como usar uma funcionalidade: S4.

--------------------------------------------------

CASO REAL – 12/07/2024

Às 14h30, a equipe de monitoramento detectou que o sistema de autenticação único (SSO) estava apresentando falhas intermitentes. Cerca de 30% das tentativas de login falhavam. O SSO é usado por todos os colaboradores da empresa e também por clientes externos para acessar o portal de autoatendimento. O portal de autoatendimento é essencial para abertura de chamados e consulta de faturas. O time de infraestrutura identificou que o problema estava relacionado a uma atualização de certificado SSL que expirou inesperadamente.

Às 14h45, o gerente de TI abriu o ticket #INC-2024-0712-001 com a seguinte descrição:

"Sistema de SSO com falhas intermitentes. 30% dos logins falham. Afeta colaboradores e clientes externos. O portal de autoatendimento está inacessível para muitos usuários. Não há workaround conhecido. A equipe de segurança está ciente. Não há indícios de vazamento de dados até o momento. Precisamos de classificação urgente."

O ticket foi classificado inicialmente como S2 pela equipe de plantão, que considerou o número de usuários afetados (30%) e a existência de workaround parcial (tentativas repetidas de login).

Às 15h10, o time de segurança enviou um e-mail:

"Assunto: Re: Ticket #INC-2024-0712-001 – Atualização

Prezados,

Confirmamos que o certificado SSL expirado pertence ao serviço de autenticação SSO. Isso significa que as conexões não estão criptografadas durante o processo de login. Embora não tenhamos detectado vazamento de dados, há risco potencial de interceptação de credenciais enquanto o certificado não for renovado. A renovação está prevista para as 18h de hoje. Até lá, recomendamos que os usuários não façam login em redes públicas.

Atenciosamente,
Equipe de Segurança da Informação"

Às 15h30, o gerente de TI encaminhou o e-mail para a equipe de plantão com a pergunta: "Considerando a política, qual é a severidade correta deste incidente?"

Às 16h, o time de infraestrutura atualizou o ticket: "Renovação do certificado concluída com sucesso. SSO operando normalmente desde as 15h50. Monitoramento contínuo por 24h."

O ticket foi encerrado às 16h05.

--------------------------------------------------

FORMULÁRIO DE ABERTURA DE TICKET (preenchido pelo gerente de TI)

Campo: Impacto no negócio
- Faturamento: O portal de autoatendimento permite consulta de faturas, mas o pagamento é feito por outro sistema que não foi afetado.
- Operação interna: 30% dos colaboradores não conseguem acessar sistemas internos via SSO.
- Clientes externos: 30% dos clientes não conseguem acessar o portal de autoatendimento.
- Segurança: Risco potencial de interceptação de credenciais, sem vazamento confirmado.
- Workaround: Tentativas repetidas de login funcionam em alguns casos; não é garantido.

Campo: Horário do incidente
- Início: 14h30 (horário comercial)
- Detecção: 14h30
- Abertura do ticket: 14h45

Campo: Classificação inicial
- S2 (justificativa: 30% dos usuários afetados, workaround parcial)

INTERNAL POLICY DOCUMENT: SOCIAL MEDIA SAFETY & COMPLIANCE
Reference ID: SM-2024-Q3-MOD-09
Effective Date: October 1, 2024
Author: Legal Compliance Team
Status: Active/Enforced

SECTION 1: GENERAL HATE SPEECH PROHIBITION
1.1 Definition: Content that promotes violence against or incites hatred toward individuals or groups based on protected characteristics (race, ethnicity, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability) is strictly prohibited.
1.2 Enforcement Threshold: Immediate removal and account suspension for severe violations. Warning system for first-time minor infractions.
1.3 Contextual Analysis: Moderators must evaluate intent, target specificity, and potential for real-world harm. Vague statements without specific targets are generally classified as 'Non-Violent Speech' unless accompanied by calls to action.

SECTION 2: EXCEPTION FOR HISTORICAL AND EDUCATIONAL CONTENT
2.1 The "Educational Exception": Users may share hate speech content if it is explicitly framed as historical documentation, academic analysis, or news reporting. This exception applies ONLY IF the following three criteria are met simultaneously:
   a) The content includes a clear, prominent disclaimer stating it is shared for educational/historical purposes.
   b) The user’s account history demonstrates no prior strikes for Violent Extremism or Direct Threats.
   c) The content does not include current, actionable instructions for violence or harassment against living individuals.
2.2 Override Clause: If any of the three criteria in Section 2.1 are NOT met, the Educational Exception is void, and Section 1.1 (General Prohibition) applies fully.

SECTION 3: RECENT UPDATE - DIRECT THREATS VS. HATRED
3.1 Amendment Note (Nov 15, 2024): In response to recent escalations, all moderation decisions involving threats against public officials now take precedence over general hate speech guidelines. 
3.2 Specificity Rule: A statement constitutes a "Direct Threat" only if it names a specific individual or clearly identifiable group AND implies immediate physical harm. Generalized anger toward political figures, even if violent in tone, is categorized under Section 1.1 but requires the "Potential Harm" assessment matrix before suspension.
3.3 Clarification on Historical Context: Sharing images of past extremist rallies is permitted under Section 2.1. However, sharing *current* recruitment materials from active terrorist organizations is ALWAYS prohibited, regardless of educational framing, per Federal Compliance Mandate FC-88.

---
CASE FILE TICKET #MOD-99821
Date Opened: November 20, 2024
Moderator Assigned: J. Rivera
Priority: High
User Handle: @HistoryBuff_88
Account Age: 4 years
Prior Strikes: 1 (Minor Infraction: Spam/Bot Behavior, resolved March 2023). No history of Violent Extremism.

SUBMITTED CONTENT DESCRIPTION:
The user posted a video titled "The Reality of 1930s Propaganda." The video consists of archival footage of Nazi rallies with original audio speeches. At the 0:45 mark, the video cuts to a modern-day clip of an anonymous neo-Nazi forum screenshot showing a list of addresses for local city council members in Seattle, WA, with the text overlay: "These traitors need to be silenced permanently."

USER COMMENT ON POST:
"Sharing this for educational purposes to show how propaganda evolved into direct targeting. Disclaimer: For academic use only."

MODERATOR NOTES:
1. Verified Account History: Clean regarding extremism. Criteria 2.1(b) is MET.
2. Verified Disclaimer: Text "For academic use only" is present in caption. Criteria 2.1(a) is MET.
3. Content Analysis: The first part is historical. The second part contains addresses of living public officials and a call for "silencing permanently," which implies physical harm.
4. Conflict Check: Does Section 2.1(c) apply? Section 2.1(c) states exception is void if content includes "current, actionable instructions for violence or harassment against living individuals."
5. Conflict Check: Does Section 3.1 apply? Section 3.1 says threats against public officials take precedence. The content includes specific addresses and a threat against them.
6. Decision Needed: Remove post, Warn user, Suspend account, or Allow with edit?

---
EMAIL THREAD EXCERPT
From: Sarah Chen (Legal)
To: J. Rivera (Mod Team)
Subject: Re: Ticket MOD-99821 Interpretation
Date: Nov 20, 2024, 2:14 PM

J,

Regarding the mix of historical and modern content. Please look closely at Section 3.3. It states that while historical images are okay, sharing *current* recruitment materials or actionable data from active groups is ALWAYS prohibited. The address list is effectively doxxing/current actionable data. Therefore, the Educational Exception (Section 2.1) cannot save this post because criterion (c) fails.

However, note Section 3.2. Is this a "Direct Threat" requiring immediate suspension, or just a violation of Section 1.1? The language "silenced permanently" is ambiguous. It could mean firing them (political silencing) or killing them. Given the inclusion of home addresses, we treat this as high-risk. 

Recommendation: Remove content immediately. Do not suspend account yet; issue a Final Warning citing Section 2.1(c) failure. If he reposts similar hybrid content, then suspend.

q1.instructions: Based on the policy documents and case facts, what is the correct enforcement action for Moderator J. Rivera?

criteria.remove_and_warn: Remove the post and issue a final warning, citing failure of the Educational Exception criteria.
criteria.suspend_immediately: Suspend the user's account immediately due to the direct threat nature of the content.
criteria.allow_with_edit: Allow the post to remain if the user edits out the modern screenshot section.
criteria.insufficient_information: The policy does not specify whether 'silenced permanently' constitutes a direct threat.

q2.instructions: Does the user meet all criteria for the 'Educational Exception' outlined in Section 2.1?

criteria.true: The user meets criteria a, b, and c.
criteria.false: The user fails at least one of criteria a, b, or c.

q3.instructions: Evaluate the severity of the violation based on the combination of Policy Section 1.1, Section 2.1, and Section 3.3.
criteria: Level 1: Minor infraction; no educational value lost, no risk to safety.
Level 2: Moderate infraction; educational exception applies partially, low risk.
Level 3: Severe infraction; educational exception voided due to current actionable data, high risk to safety.
Level 4: Critical emergency; immediate law enforcement referral required due to confirmed assassination plot.

Section 3. Priority Assignment
Every alert must be assigned exactly one priority at triage based on the highest-severity condition met, using the following ordinal scale (lowest to highest):
P4 — Informational: no policy violation; user education or tuning recommended.
P3 — Low: suspicious but unconfirmed activity with no evidence of unauthorized access; monitor or request clarification.
P2 — Medium: confirmed unauthorized or anomalous access to non-sensitive systems or data, or a confirmed policy violation without data exfiltration.
P1 — High: confirmed unauthorized access to sensitive data, confirmed malware execution on a production endpoint, or any confirmed exfiltration of internal data.
P0 — Critical: imminent or ongoing material impact to production or customer data, active ransomware, or compromise of an administrative account with domain-wide privileges.

Section 4. Escalation
P1 and P0 alerts must page the on-call security engineer within 15 minutes and notify the CISO within 60 minutes. P2 alerts are handled during business hours and must be resolved or escalated within 24 hours. P3 and P4 are queued for the next business day. An alert that initially appears P3 but later reveals unauthorized access to sensitive data is re-prioritized to P1 at the moment of discovery.

Section 5. Evidence Standard
A finding of "confirmed" requires at least two independent corroborating evidence sources (e.g., endpoint log plus badge log, or email header plus server log). A single uncorroborated source supports only "suspected" and cannot alone drive an escalation above P2.

Recebi uma solicitação de financiamento pessoal para compra de equipamento profissional (câmera e iluminação) no valor de R$ 18.000,00, parcelado em 24 meses. Vamos analisar os documentos anexados ao ticket do sistema.

RESUMO DOS DADOS DO CLIENTE (MARCO ANTÔNIO LIMA):
- Data de Nascimento: 12/05/1985 (Idade: 38 anos)
- Situação CPF: Regular
- Consulta Serasa: Não constam débitos protestados acima de R$ 500,00. Há uma restrição antiga de R$ 150,00 já baixada.
- Conta Corrente Banco Aurora: Aberta em 10/01/2022. Tempo de relacionamento atual: 21 meses e 5 dias.
- Renda Comprovada: O cliente é freelancer de fotografia. Apresentou extratos bancários dos últimos 6 meses mostrando entradas médias de R$ 4.500,00/mês. Declarou no formulário que sua renda líquida média após impostos e custos operacionais é de R$ 3.800,00.
- Histórico de Crédito Externo: Score de crédito informado pela bureau como 780 pontos. No entanto, o relatório detalhado indica que este score é baseado apenas em consultas recentes e dívidas pequenas. O histórico consolidado de contas em outros bancos mostra apenas 8 meses de atividade contínua com fluxo financeiro relevante antes desta consulta.
- Parcela Estimada: Para R$ 18.000,00 em 24 meses, a taxa anual efetiva é de 4%. A parcela calculada pelo simulador é de R$ 792,00.

OBSERVAÇÕES DA EQUIPE DE DOCUMENTOS:
- O contrato social da empresa individual do cliente foi registrado em março de 2022, mas as movimentações financeiras significativas só começaram em janeiro de 2023.
- Não há garantias reais oferecidas (colateral zero).
- O objetivo declarado é aumento de capacidade produtiva (equipamentos duráveis).

CONFLITO IDENTIFICADO:
Precisamos decidir se classificamos este caso para aprovação automática ou análise manual aprofundada. Há divergência sobre qual nível de risco aplicar devido à discrepância entre o 'score numérico alto' e a 'falta de histórico consolidado'.

Att.,
Ana B.

criteria.insuficient_informations: Não é possível calcular a capacidade de pagamento porque a política não define claramente se usa renda bruta ou líquida para freelancers.
criteria.reprovacao_limite: A parcela de R$ 792,00 excede 30% da renda líquida média aplicando-se o redutor prudencial de 20% exigido para renda variável.

criteria: Nível 1 (Baixo)
Nível 2 (Moderado)
Nível 3 (Alto)
Nível 4 (Rejeição Automática)

DOCUMENT: Reservation Change Policy & Case File

POLICY EXCERPT — Aurora Grand Hotel (effective Jan 1, 2025)

1. Standard Rate reservations may be modified up to 48 hours before check-in at no charge for date changes; one date change is allowed per reservation. A second date change incurs a $75 administrative fee.
2. Advance Purchase (nonrefundable) reservations cannot be date-changed or canceled; however, the hotel may allow a one-time courtesy date change if the request is made at least 7 days before check-in AND the new stay is within 90 days of the original check-in date. Courtesy changes are subject to availability and rate difference; any rate increase must be paid by the guest.
3. Corporate Negotiated Rate reservations: changes permitted up to 24 hours before check-in with no fee; rate remains the same for the new dates if the new dates fall within the same corporate rate season (Jun–Aug or Dec–Jan). If new dates fall outside the season, the corporate rate no longer applies and the best available rate will be quoted.
4. Group Block reservations (10+ rooms) are governed by the group contract. If the contract is silent, the Standard Rate rules apply, except that only one change is allowed regardless of timing.
5. Name changes are not date changes and are always free. Date changes requested within 48 hours of check-in are treated as cancellations and rebookings under the original rate rules.
6. Rate differences: if the new dates are more expensive, guest pays the difference; if less expensive, no refund is given for Advance Purchase and Corporate Negotiated, but Standard Rate guests receive a credit for the difference.
7. All change requests must be submitted in writing (email or ticket) and acknowledged by the hotel. Phone requests are not valid until confirmed in writing.

CASE FACTS

Reservation: #AUR-78421
Guest: Mateo Rivas
Original booking: Corporate Negotiated Rate, June 10–14, 2025 (4 nights), $189/night.
Confirmation email sent Feb 3, 2025.

Email thread:

From: Mateo Rivas <mateo.rivas@brightloop.io>
To: Aurora Grand Reservations <reservations@auroragrand.example>
Date: May 20, 2025, 9:14 AM
Subject: Change request – AUR-78421

Hello, I need to move my June stay to July 22–26, 2025. My company’s rate season is Jun–Aug, so I expect the same $189 rate. Please confirm.

— Mateo

From: Aurora Grand Reservations
To: Mateo Rivas
Date: May 20, 2025, 4:40 PM
Subject: RE: Change request – AUR-78421

Dear Mr. Rivas,
We can offer July 22–26 at the corporate rate of $189/night, subject to the change rules for your rate plan. Please reply to confirm and we will process.

— Priya, Reservations

From: Mateo Rivas
To: Aurora Grand Reservations
Date: May 21, 2025, 8:02 AM
Subject: RE: RE: Change request – AUR-78421

Confirmed, please proceed.

— Mateo

Hotel log (Reservations system):
May 21, 2025 8:05 AM — Agent noted: “Guest confirmed by email. Request is more than 24h before check-in; new dates within Jun–Aug season. Rate stays $189. Pending final approval.”
May 22, 2025 10:12 AM — System alert: “Corporate rate code BRLOOP-2025 expired on May 15, 2025. All corporate negotiated rates for Brightloop are discontinued for stays after May 31, 2025. Existing reservations with arrival before May 31 may keep rate; changes to arrivals after May 31 are not eligible for corporate rate.”
May 23, 2025 9:00 AM — Agent comment: “Guest’s original arrival June 10 is after May 31, but booking was made Feb 3. Corporate rate may or may not apply. Need policy check.”

Internal ticket #T-9921:
Priority: Normal
Opened: May 23, 2025
Subject: Rate eligibility for AUR-78421 change
Description: Guest wants July 22–26. Original corporate rate $189. Corporate code expired May 15 for new arrivals after May 31. Policy section 3 says corporate rate remains same if new dates within same season. Policy section 2 (Advance Purchase) doesn’t apply. No group contract. Standard rate rules mention 48h and $75 fee. What rate and fees apply?

Additional facts:
- Current date: May 23, 2025.
- Original check-in June 10 is 18 days away.
- New check-in July 22 is 60 days away.
- Best available rate for July 22–26 is $229/night.
- Guest has not been charged any fee yet.
- No written notice of corporate code expiration was sent to Mateo.

Question for evaluator: determine the correct routing/outcome for this change request.

q1.instructions: Which rate and fee outcome should the hotel apply to reservation #AUR-78421 for the new dates July 22–26, 2025?

criteria.corporate_rate_189_no_fee: Keep the corporate rate of $189/night, no change fee.
criteria.corporate_rate_189_plus_75: Keep the corporate rate of $189/night, but charge the $75 administrative fee.
criteria.best_available_229_no_fee: Apply the best available rate of $229/night, no change fee.
criteria.best_available_229_plus_75: Apply the best available rate of $229/night, plus the $75 administrative fee.
criteria.cancel_and_rebook: Treat as cancellation and rebooking at the best available rate.
criteria.insufficient_information: There is not enough information to determine the correct outcome.

q2.instructions: Proposition: Under the policy, Mateo's requested change must be processed as a cancellation and rebooking because it is within 48 hours of check-in.

criteria.true: The change must be processed as a cancellation and rebooking.
criteria.false: The change must not be processed as a cancellation and rebooking.

q3.instructions: Rate the appropriateness of the hotel's May 20 written response that offered “July 22–26 at the corporate rate of $189/night, subject to the change rules for your rate plan.”
criteria: Clearly correct and appropriate: the offer accurately reflects the corporate rate eligibility without conditions.
Mostly appropriate but contains a material condition that could change the rate.
Ambiguous: the response neither confirms nor denies the corporate rate.
Misleading: the response implies the corporate rate applies when it likely does not.
Clearly incorrect: the response guarantees a rate that is definitely unavailable.

q4.instructions: According to the policy, which change-related fee or credit, if any, applies to this reservation if the hotel proceeds with the July 22–26 dates at the best available rate?

criteria.no_fee_no_credit: No change fee and no credit for rate difference.
criteria.credit_for_difference: A credit for the difference between the original and new rate.
criteria.cancellation_penalty: A cancellation penalty under the original rate rules.

Assunto: Atualização do Protocolo de Registro Térmico (Versão 3.1)

Conforme a política corporativa vigente desde 01/01/2024, todos os alimentos preparados devem ser resfriados até 5°C em no máximo 6 horas após o fim da cocção. Registros manuais em papel são aceitos apenas se acompanhados de assinatura digital via tablet. Em caso de discrepância entre logs automatizados e manuais, prevalece o log com timestamp mais recente validado pelo sistema central.

CASO EM ANÁLISE: Refeição "Lasanha à Bolonhesa" produzida em 10/05/2024.
1. Log Automatizado (Sonda IoT #45): Início da cocção às 14:00. Fim da cocção às 15:30. A sonda registrou temperatura ambiente de 22°C na sala de espera. O sistema não detectou inserção imediata da lasanha na câmara fria.
2. Log Manual (Formulário P-09): Preenchido por João Costa às 18:45. Declara que a lasanha foi colocada na câmara fria às 15:35. Assinatura manual presente.

Isso contradiz o registro manual de 15:35. Considerando que o email de Ana é anterior ao meu lembrete formal e contém erro factual comprovado pelo sensor, o registro oficial deve refletir o evento físico real.

REQUISITO FINAL: Determine se a temperatura interna atingiu 5°C dentro do limite permitido, considerando que a refrigeração começou efetivamente às 17:10 (abertura confirmada pela porta) e assumindo uma taxa de resfriamento padrão de 0,8°C/minuto partindo de 60°C.

   - Se a nova tarifa for superior à original, o hóspede deve pagar a diferença integral na hora da confirmação da alteração.
   - Se a nova tarifa for inferior à original, a diferença é convertida em crédito para estadia futura, válido por 12 meses, exceto se o método de pagamento original foi cartão corporativo pré-pago.
   - A taxa administrativa de R$ 50,00 (se aplicável) é acumulada ao diferencial positivo. O diferencial negativo não gera reembolso em dinheiro.

3. CASO ESPECIAL - RESERVA CORPORATIVA PRÉ-PAGA:
   - Reservas pagas antecipadamente via faturamento corporativo (boleto único) estão sujeitas a multa de 15% sobre o valor total da reserva caso haja alteração que resulte em redução de noites ou categoria inferior.
   - Não há cobrança de taxa fixa de R$ 50,00 para estas reservas, pois o contrato corporativo isenta taxas administrativas individuais.

4. DEFINIÇÕES OPERACIONAIS:
   - 'Check-in': Data/hora de chegada prevista no sistema PMS.
   - 'Valor Total da Reserva': Soma das diárias + taxas de serviço (10%) + impostos municipais (ISS), excluído taxas de resort obrigatórias se não estiverem no pacote base.
   - 'No-show': Ausência sem aviso prévio dentro da janela de 4 dias.

---
REGISTRO DE TICKET DE SUPORTE #8842-HL
Data de Abertura: 15/05/2024 às 14:30
Cliente: Empresa TechNova Ltda. (Conta Corporativa #CN-9982)
Hóspede Responsável: Sr. João Silva
Reserva Original: Ref. HL-2024-5501
Hotel: Grand Litoral Resort & Spa
Data Check-in Original: 25/05/2024
Data Check-out Original: 28/05/2024 (3 noites)
Categoria Original: Suíte Master Vista Mar
Tarifa Original Diária: R$ 600,00
Total Original Reservado (Pré-pago): R$ 2.178,00 (Incluso ISS/Serviço). Nota Fiscal emitida em 01/05/2024.
Status Pagamento: Boletos Corporativos Liquidados em 05/05/2024.

MENSAGENS DO TICKET:

[João Silva] 15/05/2024 14:30:
"Olá, preciso alterar nossa reserva. Devido a uma mudança na agenda executiva, chegaremos um dia depois e sairemos um dia antes. Precisamos mudar para 26/05 (check-in) e 27/05 (check-out). Ou seja, apenas 1 noite. Além disso, a Suíte Master está indisponível nessa curta janela, então queremos mudar para Quarto Standard com vista lateral. A diária do Standard é R$ 350,00. Qual será o custo final?"

[Sistema Automático] 15/05/2024 14:31:
Verificação de elegibilidade:
- Data da solicitação: 15/05/2024.
- Data de Check-in Original: 25/05/2024.
- Dias até check-in original: 10 dias.
- Janela de alteração: > 7 dias (Alteração permitida).
- Tipo de pagamento: Corporativo Pré-pago (Cláusula 3 ativa).

[Agente Helena Costa] 15/05/2024 15:10:
Sr. João, recebemos sua solicitação.
Como a alteração ocorre a mais de 7 dias do check-in original, não há incidência da taxa fixa de R$ 50,00.
Contudo, como se trata de uma Conta Corporativa Pré-paga (Cláusula 3), a redução de noites e a mudança para categoria inferior (downgrade) ativam a multa administrativa de 15% sobre o Valor Total da Reserva Original.
Além disso, haverá ajuste de tarifas.
Para calcularmos o valor a ser devolvido ou retido, precisamos considerar:
1. Multa Cláusula 3: 15% de R$ 2.178,00 = R$ 326,70.
2. Novo Custo da Estadia: 1 noite x R$ 350,00 = R$ 350,00.
3. Comparação Financeira:
   Valor Pago Original: R$ 2.178,00
   Menos Multa Retida: R$ 326,70
   Saldo Disponível para Cobrir Nova Estadia: R$ 2.178,00 - R$ 326,70 = R$ 1.851,30.
   Como o novo custo (R$ 350,00) é menor que o saldo disponível após a multa, haverá reembolso parcial da diferença restante?

Nota: Em contratos corporativos pré-pagos, o excedente financeiro após a aplicação de multas contratuais é convertido em Crédito Corporativo Válido, não em dinheiro, salvo acordo especial de diretoria. O Sr. possui autorização especial para reembolso em dinheiro? Caso não, o valor residual fica como crédito.

[João Silva] 15/05/2024 16:05:
"Não tenho autorização especial para reembolso em dinheiro, prefiro manter como crédito se possível, mas quero saber o número exato do valor que sobra para eu registrar na contabilidade. E confirme se a taxa dos 10% de serviço se aplica novamente ao novo quarto standard?"

[Agente Helena Costa] 15/05/2024 16:20:
Confirmado, Sr. João. As taxas de serviço e ISS são embutidas nas tarifas divulgadas para contas corporativas fechadas. O cálculo final é:

Base de Cálculo Multa: R$ 2.178,00
Multa (15%): R$ 326,70

Custo da Nova Reserva (Standard, 1 noite): R$ 350,00

Saldo Líquido (Valor Pago - Multa - Novo Custo):
R$ 2.178,00 - R$ 326,70 - R$ 350,00 = R$ 1.501,30.

Este valor de R$ 1.501,30 será creditado na conta corporativa TechNova para uso futuro. Não haverá débito adicional, pois o custo da nova estadia foi coberto pelo saldo remanescente da original após a multa. O cliente não paga nada agora, nem recebe dinheiro. Recebe crédito.

POLÍTICA DE ACESSO A NUVEM – TI-SEG-012 (excerto relevante)

5.2. Aprovação de acesso a recursos de nuvem
5.2.1. Toda solicitação de acesso a recursos de nuvem deve ser aprovada pelo gestor direto do solicitante e pelo proprietário do recurso (Resource Owner).
5.2.2. Para acessos com privilégios elevados (roles de administrador, owner ou equivalentes), é obrigatória também a aprovação do Security Champion da unidade.
5.2.3. A aprovação do gestor direto pode ser delegada formalmente por e-mail registrado em ticket, desde que o delegado seja do mesmo departamento e tenha nível hierárquico igual ou superior ao do solicitante.
5.2.4. Solicitações de acesso temporário (menos de 7 dias corridos) estão dispensadas da aprovação do Security Champion, desde que não envolvam privilégios elevados.
5.2.5. O prazo máximo para conclusão do fluxo de aprovação é de 3 dias úteis após a abertura do ticket. Se não concluído nesse prazo, o ticket é escalado automaticamente para o Comitê de Segurança.
5.2.6. Acessos de leitura (read-only) a dados não classificados como sensíveis ou restritos podem ser aprovados apenas pelo gestor direto, dispensando o Resource Owner.

CASO: Ticket TCK-2024-5510

Aberta em: 2025-03-10 09:14 (segunda-feira)
Solicitante: Mariana Costa, Analista de Dados Sênior, Departamento de BI.

Duração solicitada: 30 dias corridos (de 2025-03-17 a 2025-04-16).
Privilégios: somente leitura (read-only).

E-mail de 2025-03-10 10:02 – Mariana para Rafael Lima:
“Rafael, abri o ticket TCK-2024-5510 para acesso de leitura ao bucket de dados restritos. Preciso para começar a análise de churn. Pode aprovar? Abs, Mariana.”

E-mail de 2025-03-10 11:30 – Rafael Lima para Mariana:
“Mariana, vou estar de férias de 12 a 26 de março. Delego minha aprovação para a Paula Souza (Coordenadora de BI, mesmo departamento, nível hierárquico superior ao seu). Já registrei isso no ticket. Boa análise!”

Comentário no ticket em 2025-03-10 11:35 – Rafael Lima:
“Delego aprovação a Paula Souza conforme e-mail. Ela pode aprovar em meu nome.”

Comentário no ticket em 2025-03-10 14:00 – Paula Souza:

2025-03-10 11:35 – Delegação registrada por Rafael Lima.
